- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for risk reversal.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >3%), model often overcorrects in next period; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- If true price deviates from 30d moving average by >2%, model is biased; adjust forecast to align with recent 7–14d mean.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from 1.00 to 0.00) triggers mean reversion; forecast should drop toward prior 10d average within 2–3 periods.
- Model tends to lag sentiment shifts by 1–2 periods; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to match sentiment momentum.
- For 30d horizon, avoid extreme outliers (±5% from 14d range); cap forecast within ±3% of recent 14d volatility band.
